holidays.name: National Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A salute to everything stacked between two slices of bread, from towering deli creations to a humble PB&J. Grab your favorite sandwich, or build a wildly over-the-top one at home.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich, born November 3, 1718. He is the man the sandwich is traditionally named after.
holidays.funFact: Legend says the Earl asked for meat tucked between bread so he could keep playing cards without greasy fingers. Others say he was simply working at his desk.

holidays.name: Cliché Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace every well-worn phrase you can think of. Today, it's fair to say that what goes around comes around, and that you should avoid clichés like the plague.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to play with overused expressions, whether they do it with a wink or by accident.
holidays.funFact: The word cliché comes from a French printing term. It referred to a metal plate that cast the same block of type over and over, which is a fitting image for a repeated phrase.

holidays.name: World Jellyfish Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the brainless, heartless, boneless wonders that have drifted through the oceans for hundreds of millions of years. Celebrate with an aquarium visit or a jellyfish documentary.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It draws attention to jellyfish and the health of the world's oceans.
holidays.funFact: Jellyfish have no brain, heart, or bones, and they have existed for more than 500 million years. That makes them older than dinosaurs and even trees.
